values: change-history
co-change
Two folders of production code that changed together in most of the commits of the less-changed one, which the history check reads when `history.coChange` is on.
Folders that keep changing together usually share knowledge that has no single owner, so every change has to touch both.
This is correlation, not proof of coupling: if they share knowledge (a format, a constant, a schema) give it one owner, and if they only ever change as one unit, merge them.

two folders of production code that changed together in at least 5 of the last 300 commits and in at least 60% of the commits of the less-changed one (only edits of production code count, and commits of more than 30 files are ignored); opt-in with `history.coChange`, never fails
Report-only: it never fails the gate.
coding-standards
baseline-expansion
A change raises an allowance in the legacy baseline (`nitpicker.legacy.json`).
The baseline records old problems so that they can shrink; raising it would hide new ones.
Fix the new sites instead of baselining them.

values.note: It has no exception: fix the sites instead of raising the allowance of the legacy inventory.

values: java
kotlin
python
callback-protocol/<rule>
A callback breaks its protocol: `source-loader-does-not-merge-published-state`, `publication-owner-does-not-commit-external-state` or `correlated-callback-declares-correlation-input`.

Callbacks that belong together keep one owner for the state they publish and declare the input that correlates them. No contract is declared by default, so the rules report only where a callback contract is configured.
Commit published state in its owner, read only bounded metadata or independent upstream snapshots in a loader, and declare the correlation input in the options.
^callback-protocol/.+$
coding-standards/callback-protocol/source-loader-does-not-merge-published-state
doc-comment-content
A doc comment that only restates its declaration name, or whose description is longer than the limit.
A comment that repeats the name adds noise; a long one belongs in names and types.

a doc comment or docstring that only restates its declaration name (a tag or section with text, such as `@param id the account` or `Args:`, says more), or a description longer than 5 lines, tags, sections and code examples not counted (TypeScript and JavaScript report it as `nitpicker/no-comments`)

values.label: restatingDocComment
values.message: This doc comment only restates <name>. ⟦Delete it, or say what the name cannot: a unit, a limit, an edge case or why.⟧

values.label: longDocComment
values.message: This doc comment's description is <lines> lines (limit <limit>). ⟦Keep the non-obvious point, a unit, a limit or an edge case, and put the rest in names and types.⟧

values: public-contract-production-use
A method of an exported interface that a production class implements, which no production code outside the implementations uses.
A contract method that production code never calls is dead surface that every implementation has to carry.
Remove the method from the interface, or call it from production code.
runtime-boundary/<rule>
A module breaks the runtime boundary of its role: `forbidden-runtime-dependency`, `forbidden-runtime-call` or `unresolved-runtime-dependency`.
Module roles keep the runtime dependencies and side effects of each layer in one direction. No role is declared by default, so the rules report only where a role is configured.
Depend on the allowed module, move the call to a module whose role may make it, and write the specifier of a dynamic import as a string literal.
^runtime-boundary/.+$
coding-standards/runtime-boundary/forbidden-runtime-call
coupling
shared-used-by-one-feature
A module under a shared root that exactly one feature reaches and nothing else uses.
`shared` is for code several features use; code with one user belongs with it.
<path> is used only by feature <feature>. ⟦Move it into <directory>.⟧
stability-direction
A package that depends on a less stable package.
Stable code that depends on volatile code breaks whenever the volatile code changes (the Stable Dependencies Principle).
Depend on an abstraction in a more stable package, or move the dependency inward. An import that exists only for the type checker is never the reported dependency.
coverage
changed-branch-coverage
A branch the change added or touched with coverage below the minimum.
Only changed code is held to coverage, so a change cannot add code that no test exercises.
Cover the branch with a test. When a branch cannot be reached from a test, accept it with an exception that names its function; it applies to that function only.
a changed branch with coverage below 95%
jacoco
coverage-py
crap
crap-coverage-unknown
A function with unknown coverage and so no CRAP score, because no test runs it.
A function no test runs cannot be scored, and is the riskiest kind.

values.label: crapCoverageUnknown
values.message: <name> has unknown coverage and no CRAP score: no test runs it. ⟦Add a test that calls it; for inline composition-root wiring, move it to a named function in adapters/ and test that.⟧

values.label: crapCoverageUnknownJava
values.message: <name> has unknown coverage and no CRAP score: JaCoCo has no data for it, so no test runs it or it is annotated @Generated. ⟦Add a test that calls it, and remove @Generated from hand-written code.⟧

values: crap-score-limit
A function whose CRAP score (its complexity combined with how little of it the tests cover) is at or above the limit.
Complex code that tests do not cover is the code most likely to break unnoticed.
CRAP score at or above 9; override with `QUALITY_CRAP_SCORE_LIMIT` (positive number) or `thresholds.crapLimit`

values.label: crapScoreLimit
values.message: <name> has CRAP <crap>; score must be below <limit>. ⟦Test its uncovered branches, or split a branchy part into its own function.⟧

values.label: crapScoreLimitCovered
values.message: <name> has CRAP <crap> although tests cover it; score must be below <limit>. ⟦Reduce its branches: split a branchy part into its own function.⟧

values: dead-code
exports
Unused export.
An export that nothing imports is dead surface; every reader has to understand it.
Remove `export`, or the declaration if nothing uses it.
files
Unused file.
Nothing imports the file, and no entry point, test or configuration reaches it.
Delete the file, or import it where it is needed.
test-only-export
An export, module or main class that only tests use (a re-export is not an import).
Code that only tests call is not part of the product, and its tests prove nothing about it.
coupling

values.label: testOnlyExport
values.message: Export <name> is only imported by tests. ⟦Remove `export`, or import it from production code.⟧

values.label: testOnlyReexport
values.message: If a host or tool loads <reexporter> instead of importing it, list it in "layout.entryPoints".⟧

values.label: testOnlyModule
values.message: Module <name> is only imported by tests. ⟦Move it to a test-support/ folder, or import it from production code.⟧

values.label: testOnlyDeclaration
values.message: <name> is only used by tests. ⟦Make it private to its module, or use it from production code.⟧

values.label: testOnlyFile
values.message: Module <name> is only used by tests. ⟦Move it beside the tests as a test helper, or use it from production code.⟧

values: types
Unused exported type.
An exported type that nothing imports is dead surface; every reader has to understand it.
Remove `export`, or the type if nothing uses it.
unlisted-dependency
An import of a package that `package.json` does not list.
An unlisted package works only by accident of what else is installed.
Add the package to the right dependencies of `package.json`.
unresolved-import
An import that resolves to no file and no package.
It fails when the code runs.
Fix the path, or install the package and list it in `package.json`.
unused-dependency
A dependency in `package.json` that nothing imports or runs.
Unused dependencies add install time and attack surface.
Remove it from `package.json`.
duplicates
duplicate-clone
A new block of code that repeats another block, also when only the names and literals differ.
Copies drift apart and each fix has to be made twice.
Extract the shared code into one function or module and call it from both places. When the copies are meant to be copies, the message names the files to add to `exclude`.
jscpd in `mild` mode, also over sources with names and literals normalized (at least 100 tokens, except code that only repeats one or two statements); any new clone fails
entry-points
public-alternative-bypass
An import that goes around the public entry point of a package.
Importing internals defeats the entry point that keeps a package replaceable.
Import from the public entry point.
mutation
mutant-nocoverage
A mutant in code that no test runs.
Code no test reaches is not protected against change.
Add a test that runs the code and asserts its result.
pit
mutmut
mutant-survived
A mutant (a small deliberate change to production code) that every test survived.
A mutant that survives shows a test that runs the code without checking what it does.
Strengthen the test so that it fails for the mutant: assert the exact value instead of only running the code. An equivalent mutant is accepted with an exception after review.
nitpicker-config
policy-loosened
A change to `nitpicker.config.json` or to a tool config that makes the gate check less than the base did.
A change that loosens the policy it is judged by would pass itself, so a person has to accept it.
Keep the base's policy and change the code until it passes: keep new code under the source roots, where the gate checks it, and fix findings instead of excluding, excepting or reclassifying the code.

values.note: It has no `exceptions` entry. Only a person reviewing the change accepts exactly these loosenings, with `--accept-policy-change=<digest>` at an interactive terminal or `NITPICKER_ACCEPT_POLICY_CHANGE=<digest>` in CI.

values: repository-hygiene
committed-binary
A committed archive or compiled binary (`gradle-wrapper.jar` is allowed).
Binaries bloat the history, cannot be reviewed and go stale.
Remove the file; fetch or build it in the build instead.
committed-build-output
A committed build output folder (`dist`, `build`, `out`, `coverage` or `target` next to a project manifest; `.next`, `.nuxt`, `storybook-static`, `.turbo` or `.parcel-cache` anywhere).
Build output is generated, so committing it creates noise and merge conflicts.
Remove the folder from version control and add it to `.gitignore`.
committed-env-file
A committed `.env` file (templates such as `.env.example` are fine).
An env file holds real secrets and values that differ per machine.
Remove the file from version control, ignore it, and commit a `.env.example` template.
committed-private-key
A committed private key: a key file, or any text file holding a private-key block.
A key in git is a leaked key.
Remove the key from the repository, rotate it, and load it from a secret store or the environment.
large-file
A committed file larger than the limit (lockfiles are exempt).
Large files bloat every clone for ever.
Keep large data outside the repository (artifact storage, Git LFS).
a file larger than 1 MB (lockfiles are exempt)
structure
class-fields-limit
A class with more instance fields than the limit.
Many fields mean a class holds state that belongs in separate types.
<name> has <value> fields (limit <limit>). ⟦Group related fields into a record or a class of their own.⟧
more than 10 instance fields in a class of the main Java sources or the Python source roots, or in a Go struct outside test files; override with `thresholds.classFields`
class-methods-limit
A class with more methods than the limit.
A class with many methods usually has more than one responsibility.
<name> has <value> methods (limit <limit>). ⟦Split it into classes by responsibility.⟧
more than 20 methods in a class of the main Java sources or the Python source roots, or on a Go type outside test files; override with `thresholds.classMethods`
component-story-missing
A component file without a story, in a package that has Storybook.
When most components have a story, a component without one is an oversight.
The JavaScript preset enforces this check only in part.

values.label: componentStoryMissing
values.message: Most components in this project have a story. ⟦Add <story> for <name>.⟧

values.label: componentStoryMissingUnenforced
values.message: <name> has no story. ⟦Add <story>.⟧ Not enforced until more than half of the components have one.

values: duplicate-definition
A used literal constant, function or type with the same name and text in two modules of a package.
Two copies of one definition drift apart.
Define it once in one module and import it where it is used.
exported-name-collision
Two different exports with one name, imported by the same module, which keeps the name for one of them.
Two things with one name make an import ambiguous to read.
Rename one of the exports.
file-lines-limit
A file longer than the limit (source and test files have separate limits).
Long files collect unrelated responsibilities and are slow to review.
File has <value> lines (limit <limit>). ⟦Split it into files by responsibility.⟧
more than 300 lines in a source file or 500 in a test file; override with `thresholds.fileLines` and `thresholds.testFileLines`
folder-depth-limit
Code nested deeper below its feature folder or root package than the limit.
Deep trees hide where code belongs and make imports long.
Flatten the tree: move the code up to the feature or package that owns it.

code more than 1 folder below `features/<feature>/<layer>/` (TypeScript), more than 4 packages below the root package (Java, Kotlin), more than 4 packages below the root package (Python) or more than 4 packages below the module root, `internal` not counted (Go); override with `thresholds.folderDepth`
folder-files-limit
A folder with more source files, or more test files, directly in it than the limit.
A flat folder of many files has no structure for a reader to follow.
Folder has <value> <kind> files directly in it (limit <limit>). ⟦Group related files into subfolders (packages in Java).⟧
more than 6 source files, or test files, directly in one folder; override with `thresholds.folderFiles`
function-control-nesting-limit
A function that nests control flow deeper than the limit.
Deep nesting makes the paths through a function hard to follow and to test.
<name> nests control flow <value> deep (limit <limit>). ⟦Return early instead of nesting.⟧
control nesting deeper than 2
function-lines-limit
A function longer than the limit.
Long functions hide several jobs in one place; agents grow them instead of splitting them.
Split it into functions named for what each part does and put new code in a new function. A function, file or class already over its limit may be edited as long as the change does not make it worse.
more than 50 lines
function-parameters-limit
A function with more parameters than the limit.
Long parameter lists are easy to call in the wrong order and tend to grow.
Group related parameters into one object (an options object, a record or a data class) instead of adding another.
more than 3 parameters
function-statements-limit
A function with more statements than the limit.
Many statements usually mean several responsibilities in one function.
<name> has <value> statements; limit is <limit>. ⟦Split by responsibility and name each part for what it checks or does.⟧
more than 15 statements
inheritance-depth-limit
A class that extends more superclasses than the limit.
Deep inheritance spreads behaviour over many classes and couples them.
<name> extends <value> classes deep (limit <limit>). ⟦Hold the shared part as a field and delegate to it instead of extending.⟧
a class more than 3 superclasses deep in the main Java sources or the Python source roots (Go has no inheritance); override with `thresholds.inheritanceDepth`
javascript-in-typescript-project
A `.js`, `.mjs`, `.cjs` or `.jsx` file in a project that has a `tsconfig.json`.
JavaScript in a TypeScript project has no type checking.
<path> is JavaScript in a TypeScript project, so its values are not type-checked. ⟦Write it as a .ts or .tsx file: <typescript>.⟧
line-length-limit
A line longer than the limit, except imports, URLs and the text of string literals.
Long lines are hard to review in a diff and hide complexity.
Line is <value> characters (limit <limit>). ⟦Break it up or extract a named value.⟧

a line longer than 120 characters, except imports, URLs and string literal text; override with `thresholds.lineLength` (Java files: the width of the formatter, 100 for google-java-format and 120 for palantir-java-format, or the `java.lineLength` convention (a Checkstyle `LineLength` max, a pin, or measured when no formatter runs); Kotlin files: detekt's)
new-icon-asset
A new icon-sized `.svg` file while an icon package is a dependency.
Icons from one package look consistent; one-off files pile up.
⟦Use an icon from <package> instead of adding <path>.⟧
redefined-library-component
A component named like one the project already renders from a dependency.
A second copy of a library component diverges from the real one.
<name> is already rendered from <package> in <count>. ⟦Use that one.⟧
sibling-copy-edit
A function or class edited so that it drifts from its same-named copy in another module while that copy is left unedited.
Editing one of two near-identical copies leaves the other with the old bug.
<name> is edited here but not in <others>, where it has almost the same code. ⟦Edit it there too, or merge the copies.⟧

a function or class edited so that it drifts from its same-named copy in another module of the package, at least 80% the same tokens before and after, while that copy is left unedited (Java and Kotlin: top-level classes and static, `object` and top-level functions)
unused-option
A property of the options parameter of an exported function that no call sets; in Kotlin, a defaulted parameter of a private or internal function that no call names or fills.
An option nobody sets is dead surface that every reader has to understand.
Option <name> is never set. ⟦Remove it, or set it from a real call (<scope>).⟧
unused-prop
A prop the project declares that no caller passes (a spread of a non-literal passes all).
An option or prop nobody sets is dead surface that every reader has to understand.
Prop <name> is never passed. ⟦Remove it, or pass it from a real caller (<scope>).⟧
test-console
test-console-output
A test file that prints console error or warn output the base run did not print.
Console noise hides real warnings and usually points at a leaked timer or an unhandled error.
Tests print new console output: <output>. ⟦Fix the cause (for example a timer that outlives the test), or allow a third-party message in "testConsole.allow" of nitpicker.config.json.⟧
test-runtime
test-runtime
no-production-runtime
A test that runs no production runtime code.
A test that never runs the code it is named for cannot fail when that code breaks.
Import and run the production code the test is about.
slow-test
A test the change adds or edits that takes longer than the limit for its kind (unit or integration).
Slow tests slow every run and are the first to be skipped; most tests should be fast unit tests.
Make the test fast: inject a clock or a fake instead of waiting, or move it to the integration tests, which have a higher limit.
a test the change adds or edits taking more than 5 s (unit) or 30 s (integration); override with `thresholds.unitTestSeconds` and `thresholds.integrationTestSeconds`
type-only-production-dependency
A test whose only link to production code is a type-only import.
A type import proves nothing at runtime, so the test cannot fail when the code breaks.
